title: Goose: 32 source-backed Search, GEO and agent-web opportunities
scope: Research candidate decisions, NOT automatically active advice or publisher instructions.

method.evidenceBoundary: Documented provider features and explicit experiments; no causal Search-ranking claim, invented owner evidence or recommendation-count KPI.
method.priorityOrder: P0 source credibility and first proof; P1 only where real owner evidence or eligibility exists; P2 conditional trials or research watches.
method.privacyRule: Raw owner Search Console/analytics logs, queries, personal data and private project artifacts stay outside public Goose research.
method.existingCoverage: Cards explicitly say what Goose already implements. This research does not silently add duplicate first-class engines or promote unproven tactics.

opportunities.title: Fix the OpenAI publisher-documentation source of truth
opportunities.insight: The old OpenAI publisher FAQ URL presently redirects to an unrelated retired-browser article. The current crawler documentation separately describes search, training, user-triggered and ads access.
opportunities.action: Make the active watch source point to OpenAI's crawler documentation; keep the old link as historical evidence and review the Atlas-dependent advice before representing it as current.
opportunities.check: Verify the new URL resolves to OAI-SearchBot/GPTBot/ChatGPT-User/OAI-AdsBot definitions; flag old Atlas/Apps claims as due for re-review rather than quietly transferring them.
opportunities.measure: Count recommendations whose live cited sources match the claims; prevent source-redirect incidents, not promise indexing.
opportunities.skip: Do not bulk-replace the old URL under referral or Atlas statements with crawler docs that cannot substantiate them.

opportunities.title: Replace generated-looking advice with inspected decisions
opportunities.insight: Google's 1 October 2026 update adds quality-rater context around low-effort, low-originality and low-value material. Rewording every headline is less important than giving readers something specific to decide or try.
opportunities.action: Select a small sample of the highest-seen Goose advice and target-site pages. Require one distinct useful action, owner-valid example, evidence boundary, reason not to use it and concise human explanation. Record real defects and corrections.
opportunities.check: Review original vs updated pages with user, specialist, editor and skeptic roles. Check no invented first-hand experience or claims, and preserve non-changes.
opportunities.measure: Page-specific query fit and useful continuation where owner evidence exists; otherwise editorial pass/fail only.
opportunities.skip: Do not equate lower AI-text scores or higher keyword density with search improvement.

opportunities.title: Review titles, descriptions, alt text and structured data together
opportunities.insight: Google explicitly says factual AI-output review includes metadata, not just article body text. An answer can be accurate in a paragraph but misleading in a snippet or image description.
opportunities.action: Add a bounded metadata-to-visible-facts editorial comparison to the current publication review for pages revised with AI assistance; include title, meta description, alt, JSON-LD claims and canonical job.
opportunities.check: On sampled built pages, reject invented product availability, author, review, results or attributes. Compare against the visible source of truth.
opportunities.measure: Material false claims removed and Search appearance parity checks passed; no ranking promise.
opportunities.skip: Do not auto-generate alternate metadata from unverified page summaries.

opportunities.title: Publish one original, reproducible evidence asset instead of more generic tips
opportunities.insight: Google emphasizes non-commodity information. For Goose, a clear test of a real claim is more useful than publishing another list of GEO tactics.
opportunities.action: On one existing canonical resource, add a small real repeatable experiment: question, baseline, original sample, exact method, observation, negative cases and a practical decision. Review permissions before exposing data.
opportunities.check: Verify source and final deployment refs, copyright/consent, reproducer and an independently understandable result; keep failures.
opportunities.measure: Owner query/page discovery, genuine reuse or citations where measurable, and a real keep/revise/stop decision.
opportunities.skip: Never manufacture survey respondents, third-party endorsements or a fabricated AI-citation gain.

opportunities.title: Compare Bing grounding queries with the actual cited canonical pages
opportunities.insight: Bing AI Performance exposes a grounding-query/page map, which can show whether a page is being cited for the task it really serves. The report is aggregated and can be partial.
opportunities.action: If the owner has Bing access, import a bounded query-page pair set, map stable page IDs, note provider scope and keep a review queue for mismatched intent or repeated citations.
opportunities.check: Compare raw pair mapping to cited page state and visible factual support; preserve nonreturned queries and sampling limits.
opportunities.measure: New relevant citations/grounding-query families in a later comparable period, separated from traffic and brand mentions.
opportunities.skip: Do not claim any specific prompt, model answer, ranking or causality from aggregated grounding labels.

opportunities.title: Audit four OpenAI crawler roles against actual edge responses
opportunities.insight: OpenAI's bot documentation separates OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User and OAI-AdsBot, with IP lists; a robots.txt-only test is not proof that CDN/WAF challenges allow real retrieval.
opportunities.action: For sites wanting ChatGPT discovery, reconcile publisher choice per bot with robots.txt, real WAF/CDN settings and independently observed requests from documented IP ranges; keep search/training/ads/user actions distinct.
opportunities.check: Check verified bot IPs, allowed public routes, HTTP/noindex, challenge/403 and intentionally protected paths. Use limited non-spoofed evidence.
opportunities.measure: Actual eligible fetches and separately observed ChatGPT referrals or mentions; no universal AI access score.
opportunities.skip: Do not disable firewalls wholesale, turn on training to gain search visibility or assume user-triggered ChatGPT-User is Search indexing.

opportunities.title: Use Bing AI intent buckets to choose a better answer format
opportunities.insight: Bing's 2026 preview classifies grounding contexts such as research, planning, local and commercial. That may reveal a mismatch between a cited page's goal and its actual answer.
opportunities.action: On one active owned site with enough cited pages, group the actual provider intent labels; select one page whose published content can genuinely answer a different stage or task without creating an extra URL.
opportunities.check: Review mislabeled/ambiguous intent manually; inspect page usefulness and any later cited page/query pairs.
opportunities.measure: Query/page fit on a frozen Bing intent slice, not assumed market size.
opportunities.skip: Skip when no Bing owner observations exist; preview labels are not reliable for every niche.

opportunities.title: Build a small topical opportunity map from Bing's own citation topics
opportunities.insight: Bing Topics groups AI grounding queries into subject clusters. For small niche sites, this can reveal whether original evidence spans the actual user task.
opportunities.action: Map provider topic labels to existing canonical resource pages and authentic subject boundaries. Improve an existing information gap before considering a new page.
opportunities.check: Check manually that provider topics are coherent; retain ambiguous/mixed labels and do not change frozen query experiments retroactively.
opportunities.measure: Coverage and reuse of distinct existing topic/job pages by later provider citations.
opportunities.skip: Do not mass-generate one page per topic or mistake provider topic classifications for ranking authority.

opportunities.title: Track Citation Share only within the same grounding query
opportunities.insight: Bing's new Citation Share is the share of observed citations for a specific grounding query, not share of AI traffic or a universal visibility score.
opportunities.action: Freeze up to 10 owner-observed relevant grounding queries and compare their Bing-native Citation Share at comparable intervals alongside raw citation counts and page IDs.
opportunities.check: Verify query-scoped denominator, preview availability, dates and changes in the observed query mix.
opportunities.measure: Within-query Citation Share trend plus citation count and cited-page coverage; avoid cross-surface sums.
opportunities.skip: Don't rank unrelated queries, providers or businesses by a blended citation percentage.

opportunities.title: Use Bing Compare to prevent selective screenshot-based success stories
opportunities.insight: Bing Compare overlays earlier and later periods for supported AI citation data. A chart moving upward cannot identify the cause.
opportunities.action: Record a frozen current/previous window, actual cited pages and exposure context. Include zero, flat and negative examples and known releases/outages.
opportunities.check: Check consistent page/query scope and finality/lag; preserve provider sampling warnings.
opportunities.measure: Comparable Bing-native citation trend with absolute denominators, no automatic treatment win.
opportunities.skip: Don't use a prior period with different eligibility or a changed query set as a causal control.

opportunities.title: Keep Google's ordinary Web and generative Search reports as separate populations
opportunities.insight: Google AI Overviews and AI Mode reporting has provider-specific exposure semantics. Goose's current first proof uses classic Web Search, which cannot be relabeled as AI citations.
opportunities.action: Check owner-side generative report availability and reporting dimensions separately. Keep missing as unavailable; preserve scope, date/time zone and provider semantics.
opportunities.check: Re-run the existing Google import on an actual supplied report only; verify API/CSV columns before labeling impressions.
opportunities.measure: Provider-native AI exposure separately from classic Web, Bing citations and useful sessions.
opportunities.skip: Do not infer a ChatGPT/Bing referral or a specific AI answer from Google's impressions.

opportunities.title: Check Cloudflare's September Search / Agent / Training defaults
opportunities.insight: Cloudflare separates Search, Agent and Training behaviors. New domain defaults changed in September 2026 and can affect multi-purpose crawlers.
opportunities.action: For sites actually behind Cloudflare, compare intended role policy with the account's effective crawler settings and WAF rules; record host/path and customer choice.
opportunities.check: Inspect live settings and verified response logs before changing a rule, especially ad-serving pages and multi-purpose bots.
opportunities.measure: Verified allowed/blocked crawler requests by role, not guessed ChatGPT Search traffic.
opportunities.skip: Do not recommend unblocking all AI bots or altering a site that is not on Cloudflare.

opportunities.title: Use Cloudflare path patterns and referral paths to find broken discovery loops
opportunities.insight: Cloudflare AI Crawl Control now surfaces request patterns, bytes and AI referral paths; high crawler activity in one section without useful visits calls for diagnosis, not applause.
opportunities.action: Compare the real top crawler-request URL families, response status/bytes, and AI-origin referral landing sections with the site's actual task priority.
opportunities.check: Verify provider read permissions, bot-role labels, stable periods and sample disclosure; do not infer unique users from requests.
opportunities.measure: Meaningful referral landings and supported task continuations where measured, separately from crawler bandwidth.
opportunities.skip: Do not use aggregate request volume as an authority score or scrape privacy-protected logs.

opportunities.title: Test Content Signals with an actual compatible consumer
opportunities.insight: Cloudflare Browser Run's crawl endpoint has an enforceable reference/full content-use mode, but this is a provider-specific consumer capability, not a universal search requirement.
opportunities.action: If publisher/consumer policies require it, run a tiny authorized crawl with contentUse=reference and, where policy allows, contentUse=full; verify allowed/rejected requests and the effective directive.
opportunities.check: Check the robots content-use directive, resulting status and source permission before/after, without bypassing policy.
opportunities.measure: Correct rights-policy enforcement for that one consumer; no Search rank or ChatGPT citation metric.
opportunities.skip: Never present Cloudflare's use directive as an IETF final standard or universal Google policy.

opportunities.title: Track IETF AIPREF Content-Usage header and robots attachment as a draft
opportunities.insight: The IETF AIPREF attachment and vocabulary are active Internet-Drafts, not RFCs; they define how publishers may express usage preferences distinct from crawler access.
opportunities.action: Keep a version-pinned compatibility matrix for Content-Usage HTTP/robots signals and the precise draft revision; only prototype on a test site when the real publisher rights decision exists.
opportunities.check: Check the current IETF working-group revision and consumer support; ensure no contradiction with existing robots, contracts or actual licensing.
opportunities.measure: Protocol interoperability in a compatible consumer, not discoverability uplift.
opportunities.skip: Do not automatically emit draft fields across all target sites or confuse rights preferences with guaranteed enforcement.

opportunities.title: Add a truthful video creator identity to genuine watch pages
opportunities.insight: September 2026 Google VideoObject guidance documents creator support and author as an alternative. A real video needs the correct actual creator, not an invented personal byline.
opportunities.action: On a genuinely published video, align VideoObject creator/author with the public brand/person credited on the watch page and actual media rights; no source changes for pages without a video.
opportunities.check: Rich Results Test, visible credit, canonical video/watch URL and playable media inspection.
opportunities.measure: Valid video page coverage and organic video discovery, never guaranteed video placement.
opportunities.skip: Skip for text-only guides, fictional brands, unverified authorship or unreleased videos.

opportunities.title: Verify VideoObject interactionStatistic uses supported measured actions
opportunities.insight: Google clarified supported VideoObject interaction counters. Fake view counts are an avoidable trust failure in sites that auto-fill schema.
opportunities.action: Only publish InteractionCounter data backed by the video host's actual metric and supported interaction type; otherwise omit it.
opportunities.check: Validate the interaction type, actual counts and disclosure of their scope, then compare visible facts.
opportunities.measure: Data parity and video appearance eligibility, not rank.
opportunities.skip: Never synthesize engagement from page views or a text reader count.

opportunities.title: Turn a genuinely useful video into answer-level key moments
opportunities.insight: Google supports Clip and SeekToAction on real watch pages. A practical section marker can help someone jump to the moment needed for a task.
opportunities.action: For one real published lesson/demo with clear segments, publish accurate key-moment labels/timestamps and working deep links; retain readable text/context.
opportunities.check: Play each segment URL on mobile, keyboard and browser; validate Clip/SeekToAction and indexable watch page.
opportunities.measure: Actual video deep-link engagement and separately observed Search appearances if available.
opportunities.skip: Do not add chapters to static images, nonexistent training videos or inaccessible recordings.

opportunities.title: Choose one original useful visual and reconcile preferred thumbnails
opportunities.insight: Google documents og:image and page schema as sources for preferred thumbnails. Image eligibility is different from the page's eligibility and different from Discover distribution.
opportunities.action: On a page whose visual genuinely explains the task, use a meaningful high-quality image with accessible alt, image URL, correct rights and consistent og:image/structured data. Make sure the preview works at different crops.
opportunities.check: Inspect image fetch, actual dimensions, rights, rendered HTML, max-image-preview policy and mobile crop.
opportunities.measure: Image Search/Discover appearances where exposed, separately from Web Search sessions.
opportunities.skip: No decorative logos as giant Discover hero art and no promise of Discover placement.

opportunities.title: Measure social and video content in Search Console separately from site pages
opportunities.insight: Google documented Search Console platform properties for supported social/video accounts. Distribution can happen on a platform page even when the owned-domain page is still new.
opportunities.action: For actual owned publishing channels, verify property access and inspect platform content discoverability; connect reports by canonical public topic only when evidence supports it.
opportunities.check: Record provider/property scopes, canonical URLs and distinct date windows before cross-channel interpretation.
opportunities.measure: Platform content impressions and referral/return activity where measured, not owned-site organic clicks.
opportunities.skip: Do not add social accounts just to fill a dashboard or double count site and platform impressions.

opportunities.title: Use a real Google Search profile badge when a brand profile is claimed
opportunities.insight: Google's new Search profile badge can guide people to a claimed creator or publisher Search profile. It is a distribution control, not a link scheme.
opportunities.action: For a project with an actually claimed Search profile and useful cross-platform content, add an accessible, correctly attributed optional link or official badge near the real publisher identity.
opportunities.check: Verify the claimed profile resolves, correct brand attribution, accessible touch target and no unintended disclosure of a personal maintainer.
opportunities.measure: User-follow/return engagement where provider data is available; no ranking promise.
opportunities.skip: Skip unclaimed profiles, private creator identities and sites without a real follow use case.

opportunities.title: Apply Preferred Sources only to eligible domains with a repeat readership
opportunities.insight: Google's 2026 preferred-source button supports Top Stories and potential AI Overview/Mode badges, but the selection tool only supports domain/subdomain identities, not a subdirectory URL.
opportunities.action: Check an actual owned domain in the source preferences tool first; where available and editorially useful, trial one localized interactive button or text deep link on an article hub.
opportunities.check: Verify eligibility of the exact domain, user-initiated flow, return navigation, mobile accessibility, and no false implication that the site is already preferred.
opportunities.measure: Observed reader follow/return behavior and publisher repeat discovery, not a generalized AI ranking score.
opportunities.skip: Do not show an inert button on the Goose GitHub Pages subdirectory or guarantee AI inclusion.

opportunities.title: Gate EEA aggregator opportunities on actual vertical-search business status
opportunities.insight: Google added local-business queries to EEA aggregator units in September 2026; participation is for eligible approved Vertical Search Services with meaningful data and quality requirements.
opportunities.action: Only for a real travel/product/local-business aggregator serving EEA customers, review eligibility and the direct provider application path. Keep this as a conditional business opportunity in Goose.
opportunities.check: Verify entity type, EEA consumer context, provider approval, available feed data and evidence of actual search unit appearance.
opportunities.measure: Accepted integration and genuine referrals on the applicable vertical unit.
opportunities.skip: Not applicable to a general knowledge blog, Ptichi, or Vedokrok merely because it has many pages.

opportunities.title: Check direct-supplier eligibility separately from aggregator participation
opportunities.insight: Google's supplier unit can feature direct businesses alongside EEA aggregators. It may draw from crawlable web data and, where applicable, supplier feeds.
opportunities.action: For real EEA direct hotel, flight, transport, local-service or merchant clients, separate supplier facts from aggregator feeds; review availability, actual service areas and source ownership.
opportunities.check: Verify geography, business type, directly accessible data and supplier-unit presence if reported.
opportunities.measure: Provider-native contacts or bookings attributable to the qualifying service, not a universal badge.
opportunities.skip: Don't confuse a local-direct supplier with a Vertical Search Service or create an empty feed for irrelevant sites.

opportunities.title: Qualify for Google's new UGC Fresh Data Program before proposing its API
opportunities.insight: Google announced a dedicated fresh UGC ingestion pipeline on 8 October 2026, but limits it to substantial authentic public UGC platforms with moderation, creator profiles, quality/volume and technical readiness.
opportunities.action: Add a yes/no eligibility decision when Goose reviews an actual large forum/social platform; only eligible applicants should pursue OAuth/JSON-LD and minute-level updates.
opportunities.check: Review independent user authorship, public stable URLs, moderation, user volume, engagement counter freshness and acceptance status.
opportunities.measure: Eligible approved integration processing/quality, not generalized organic indexing speed.
opportunities.skip: Do not advise standard blogs or authored content sites to use it; it is not the general Indexing API.

opportunities.title: Offer a discovery feed through OpenAI ACP only for approved merchants
opportunities.insight: OpenAI's 2026 agentic commerce program uses structured merchant feeds for more accurate ChatGPT shopping discovery, but onboarding is currently approval-gated.
opportunities.action: For an actual eligible e-commerce owner, review merchant approval, access, canonical product identity and update cadence before building an export.
opportunities.check: Check live scheme eligibility, authorization, publicly accessible real product/image URLs and accuracy of price/availability.
opportunities.measure: Feed acceptance and separately observed product discovery/merchant visits; not an organic site ranking promise.
opportunities.skip: Do not build ACP feeds for non-commerce websites or present partner onboarding as generally open.

opportunities.title: Use stable ACP product IDs and validated variant-specific facts
opportunities.insight: OpenAI specifies a Stable file upload schema; its Draft version is not production supported. IDs, variants and required fields need real product data, not LLM-generated placeholders.
opportunities.action: For an approved partner, validate stable item_id, brand, seller, title, description, canonical URL, image, stock and money, with distinct variants and stable parent/offer identity.
opportunities.check: Compare each feed row to real public product and stock truth, schema required-field checks and production Stable version; never reuse IDs.
opportunities.measure: Reduced feed errors and accurate discovered variant representation where accepted.
opportunities.skip: Do not ship the draft schema into production or invent GTIN, reviews, seller and availability.

opportunities.title: Separate full catalog snapshots from fast stock/promotion deltas
opportunities.insight: OpenAI recommends daily complete feed snapshots with later API updates; inventory and promotions can change during the day. A stale cheap price destroys user trust even when an AI recommendation appears.
opportunities.action: For supported partner integrations, use a stable complete catalog plus permitted incremental upserts, keeping promotion feeds and timestamps in their documented channel.
opportunities.check: Detect stale prices/availability by comparison with canonical commerce backend; run rollback and idempotency tests.
opportunities.measure: Feed freshness and actual order eligibility, not AI citation or search rank.
opportunities.skip: Skip if no authorized commerce backend or the partner has not been granted the required API/feed access.

opportunities.title: Keep ChatGPT ad feeds separate from organic product discovery
opportunities.insight: OpenAI publishes dedicated ads feed and OAI-AdsBot landing-page checks; ad beta eligibility is different from ACP organic discovery.
opportunities.action: On a retailer deliberately running ChatGPT ads, verify the ads-specific schema and crawlable landing pages with OAI-AdsBot and separate paid-vs-organic reporting.
opportunities.check: Inspect live landing path, verified bot accessibility, forbidden categories and accurate advertising disclosures.
opportunities.measure: Ad approval and paid attributed visits/conversions, never a claim that buying ads boosts organic recommendation.
opportunities.skip: Do not treat ads feed upload as organic ChatGPT inclusion or confuse OAI-AdsBot with GPTBot.

opportunities.title: Validate 2026 Product.category and sale-price effective dates
opportunities.insight: Google documented Product.category mapping and Offer sale validity windows in 2026. These are real data integrity issues when catalog offers change, not shortcuts for editorial pages.
opportunities.action: For an actual merchant, align feed, public listing and structured Product/Offer category, currency and sale start/end timestamps from one authoritative commerce backend.
opportunities.check: Rich Results Test, feed checks, time boundary tests and price parity after the promotion expires.
opportunities.measure: Merchant listing validity and order-quality support; no generic GEO uplift.
opportunities.skip: Skip if the site has no authentic offers, prices or eligible Product pages.

opportunities.title: Pilot declarative WebMCP only on a real useful form
opportunities.insight: Chrome 149+ documents a WebMCP origin trial and a declarative API. Tools make browser-side tasks more understandable but cannot be discovered before a browser visits the page.
opportunities.action: Choose one actual low-risk form flow whose native labels, validation and keyboard behavior are already good; trial WebMCP as an enhancement behind a browser support gate.
opportunities.check: Compare real task completion with and without the trial; do not expose hidden server actions or confuse tool discovery with consent.
opportunities.measure: Verified completion rate/accuracy for that one agent task with human oversight, not indexing or ranking.
opportunities.skip: No fake web tools for actions that do not exist; retain ordinary HTML fallback and permission boundaries.

opportunities.title: Build adversarial task evaluations for browser-agent WebMCP tools
opportunities.insight: Chrome includes debugging and agent evaluation guidance. Success depends on correct tool choice, argument constraints and resistance to unintended side effects, not a positive static metadata count.
opportunities.action: For a genuine opt-in agent workflow, freeze 5 representative tasks and 5 adversarial cases: injection, scope, duplicate call, rollback/confirmation, and denied access. Include no-WebMCP fallback.
opportunities.check: Inspect DevTools schemas, per-task receipts, user confirmation and the absence of surprise mutations or data leaks.
opportunities.measure: Task-completion correctness and safety failure count, not a search readiness score.
opportunities.skip: Do not claim an origin-trial tool improves AI Search visibility or permit writes merely because a model requested them.

opportunities.title: Use policy-aware, incremental fetch checks instead of repeated bulk crawling
opportunities.insight: Cloudflare Browser Run /crawl can use sitemap scope, static mode, and modifiedSince/maxAge to limit repeat work; the content-use directive is now enforced in compatible consumers.
opportunities.action: Where the owner already authorizes Cloudflare Browser Run, test a small unchanged-page snapshot vs a changed-page snapshot, with explicit max pages and content-use mode.
opportunities.check: Confirm robots/Content Signals consent, bounded URL inclusion, matched bytes, retry handling and no forced full crawl.
opportunities.measure: Coverage of materially changed URLs per request/cost while preserving evidence quality.
opportunities.skip: Don't substitute crawler output for Google indexing or introduce paid crawling into no-budget projects.

opportunities.title: Fail review when cited platform guidance redirects to a different topic
opportunities.insight: A source redirect can turn yesterday's well-supported advice into an unrelated citation. Goose has a current example involving a publisher FAQ and retired-browser help page.
opportunities.action: Enhance the existing Trend Radar source review process with a redirect-topic/manual confirmation step, keeping exact URL, observed destination, source class and revision date.
opportunities.check: Assert no automatic WATCH-to-ADOPT promotion; produce a review-required alert with before/after source role rather than replacing every source string automatically.
opportunities.measure: Number of stale source-backed claims caught before publication; preserve false alarms and source reachability errors.
opportunities.skip: Don't infer a recommendation is false merely because a URL moved; reverify the specific mechanism at an appropriate primary replacement source.

outcomeRule: Use a frozen provider-specific cohort, actual deployment parity, and a later reviewed keep/revise/stop decision. Retain no-change and negative observations.
stopRule: Do not ship commerce/UGC/local/video/WebMCP provider features on sites lacking the actual qualifying product, media, user action, region or authorized account.
